title: Do the lithium-ion cell designs found with a fast model still win under the full porous-electrode model?
lede: re-scoring 49 designs from energy-cell under PyBaMM's full DFN model instead of SPMe: rank correlation 0.86 at cycle 100, the SPMe winner is 3rd of 45 and still +38% over the reference cell (+31% under SPMe), DFN reports about 19 Wh/kg more on average, and SPMe fails to cycle 3 designs DFN handles (modelled, stack level)
summary: Takes the first next step of energy-cell: the 49 designs it logged (baseline, each search run's best, 36 spread over the SPMe ranking, 3 SPMe failures) are re-scored with the same parameters, protocol and mass model under the full Doyle-Fuller-Newman model. Over the 45 designs both models cycled, the cycle-100 Wh/kg rank correlation is 0.86 (0.93 at beginning of life); the SPMe winner (143.4 Wh/kg) is 3rd of 45 under DFN (160.9 vs 163.0 for the DFN best) and beats the reference cell by 38% under DFN against 31% under SPMe. DFN gives more energy for nearly every design (mean +18.6 Wh/kg), with gaps up to 127 Wh/kg, and the SPMe plateau is not flat under DFN. Limits: one cell, one parameter set, 49 designs chosen to spread over the SPMe ranking; both models share the same degradation parameters and neither is validated against measured data; stack-level mass only. Every input comes from energy-cell and PyBaMM's OKane2022 set.
